drhp.business: CMR Green processes, manufactures and sells recycled aluminium alloys (in ingot and liquid form), zinc alloy ingots and segregated furnace-ready scrap of stainless steel, copper, brass, zinc, lead and magnesium, and also produces recycled aluminium billets. It recycles used beverage-can scrap and procures aluminium scrap domestically and globally. Customers are primarily automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers, served through 13 recycling facilities across India.

drhp.expansion: With new plants in Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh) and Odisha, CMR Green is moving beyond its cast alloy base into the extrusion and rolled aluminium alloy segments. Management states entry into extrusion expands the serviceable market by a further 0.34 million MT and entry into rolled alloys by a further 0.59 million MT. The East India facility (Sambalpur, Odisha) began trial production in February 2025. As of June 30, 2025 the 13 recycling facilities operated at a combined actual production capacity of 605,850 MT.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration into raw-material sourcing: the Company procures aluminium-based and other metal scrap both domestically and overseas from around 198 global suppliers across 73 countries (spanning Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas), with a dedicated US sourcing presence through a wholly owned subsidiary; key suppliers include Sims Global Commodities, EMR USA Holdings, European Metal Recycling, Schnitzer Steel (Radius Recycling), Stemin S.P.A., Indra Recycling and Gemini Corporation. India-sourced raw materials rose to 26.85% of purchases in FY25 (FY24: 19.69%, FY23: 19.37%), with the balance imported (FY25: 73.15%). Forward integration toward customers: manufacturing facilities are established adjacent to or on customer premises (customers have on occasion leased land to the Company) to supply liquid/molten aluminium via patented road-transport technology within an approximately 20-25 km radius on a just-in-time basis (started adjacent-facility liquid supply in 2008 and road-transport supply since November 2013); 13 plants cover major OEM automotive clusters across India. Strategic technology/JV integration through joint ventures with Toyota Tsusho Corporation (since 2012), Nikkei MC Aluminium (since 2012) and Nippon Light Metal (since 2025); subsidiaries CMRN (74% held, with Nikkei) and CMRT (70% held, with Toyota Tsusho), and Nippon Light Metal's 20% investment in CMR NLM Eco for wrought-alloy / low-carbon billet recycling.

market_position.basis: Leading non-ferrous metal recycler in terms of installed capacity as of March 31, 2025 and highest market share in the Indian secondary aluminium market in terms of revenue from operations for Fiscal 2025 amongst peer companies (Source: ICRA Report); installed capacity around 4 times the nearest domestic competitor in recycled aluminium. Largest supplier of recycled liquid aluminium by turnover in Fiscal 2025. Market share of ~42-45% in terms of volume sold in the cast alloy segment pertaining to the automotive industry for FY2025. Ranks among the largest players in the global aluminium recycling industry in terms of installed capacity as of March 31, 2025.

strengths: Leading recycler in the domestic aluminium recycling industry in India with significant entry barriers and positioned as a critical enabler of the aluminium industry's decarbonization imperative; installed capacity around 4 times the nearest domestic competitor as of March 31, 2025.
Leading supplier of liquid aluminium alloy, ranking as the largest supplier of recycled liquid aluminium by turnover in Fiscal 2025.
Strong and diversified supplier base for sourcing raw materials, procuring metal scrap from around 198 global suppliers across 73 countries (excluding India) spanning six continents.
Long-standing relationships with customers comprising Tier 1 companies and OEMs, many for the last ten Fiscals.
Strategic alliances through joint ventures with Toyota Tsusho Corporation (since 2012), Nikkei MC Aluminium (since 2012) and Nippon Light Metal (since 2025).

Facilities, technology, quality processes and engineering expertise, with recycling operations at 13 strategically located facilities in India and installed capacity of 6,05,850 MTPA as of June 30, 2025.
Experienced and qualified management team with a people-focused culture; Chairman and Managing Director Mohan Agarwal has over 31 years of experience in the aluminium alloys recycling industry.

Environment friendly business supported by green technologies and processes with focus on ESG, holding the 6th highest S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA) score amongst companies in the aluminium industry scored by S&P Global.

overview.business_model: The Company processes, manufactures and sells aluminium alloys (in ingot and liquid form), zinc alloy ingots and segregated furnace ready scrap of stainless steel, copper, brass, zinc, lead and magnesium, among others. It recycles used beverage can scrap and other metal scrap procured both domestically and from overseas markets to fulfil new metal requirements of primary producers. Its customers primarily include original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and Tier 1 companies in the automotive manufacturing sector. It operates through 13 strategically located recycling units.

genesis.founding_story: Incorporated as 'Grand Metal Industries Private Limited' pursuant to a certificate of incorporation dated August 23, 2005 issued by the Assistant Registrar of Companies, National Capital Territory of Delhi and Haryana. On conversion to a public limited company the name was changed to 'Grand Metal Industries Limited' (fresh certificate dated May 28, 2020), and subsequently to 'CMR Green Technologies Limited' (certificate dated August 11, 2021).

internal_operational.detail: A significant proportion of revenue is derived from a limited number of customers; loss of or reduced demand from top customers could materially affect the business. Company served 112, 100 and 101 customers in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 for sale of aluminium and zinc alloys.
internal_operational.title: Customer concentration

internal_operational.detail: Company relies heavily on two key products; a shift in demand or availability of substitutes could adversely affect margins. Intends to diversify into aluminium billets and used beverage cans recycling but no assurance of market acceptance.
internal_operational.evidence: Liquid aluminium alloys + aluminium alloy ingots = 78.42% (Rs 52,256.01 mn) FY25, 76.95% (Rs 45,759.97 mn) FY24, 73.13% (Rs 42,821.65 mn) FY23 of revenue from operations excluding export incentives. Liquid alloys alone 43.14% FY25; ingots 35.28% FY25.

internal_operational.detail: Company relies on short-term purchase orders with no firm commitment on pricing or long-term contracts; orders may be amended or cancelled prior to finalisation, exposing it to volume/price fluctuations.

strategy_growth.detail: Company lacks a diversified product line/customer base and is over-reliant on certain products; venturing into new products/segments involves unproven know-how, unreliable technology and inexperienced staff with no assurance of success.

strategy_growth.title: Inability to successfully diversify product offerings

strategy_growth.detail: Highly competitive industry; competitors may have greater resources, better technology, better raw-material access or may influence suppliers/customers. Low capital intensity increases threat of new entrants; liquid metal cannot be transported beyond 25-30 km limiting economies of scale.
strategy_growth.evidence: Per ICRA, Company ranks among the largest players in global aluminium recycling by installed capacity (as of 31st March 2025), is the leading non-ferrous metal recycler by installed capacity, and has the highest market share in the Indian secondary aluminium market by FY2025 revenue among peers.
strategy_growth.title: Competition in the recycled metals industry

concerns_observed: Structurally thin, pass-through economics: cost of raw materials consumed was ~88.24% of revenue in FY25 (89.22% FY24, 89.33% FY23), leaving an EBITDA margin of only ~4.56% and a PAT margin of ~2.33% in FY25; there are no firm long-term customer contracts (short-term purchase orders only) and automakers pursue systematic annual price reductions.

Negative operating cash flow in FY25: net cash used in operating activities was about (Rs 92.00 cr) in FY25 versus CFO of Rs 74.10 cr (FY24) and Rs 610.90 cr (FY23), despite reported PAT of Rs 155.04 cr - a working-capital drain (trade receivables Rs 787.57 cr, inventory ~Rs 827 cr at FY25) that widens the gap between accounting profit and cash.

Rising leverage: total borrowings climbed from Rs 368.19 cr (FY23) to Rs 498.65 cr (FY24) to Rs 894.03 cr (FY25), i.e. from 10.99% to 22.72% to 31.75% of total assets; borrowings were Rs 906.65 cr as of June 30, 2025 at interest rates of 7.30%-10.36%, with several facilities repayable on demand and past one-day payment delays noted.

Import and currency dependence: 73.15% of raw-material/traded-goods purchases were imported in FY25 (USA the top source at 47.55%), on spot pricing with only partial forward-contract hedging, exposing margins to scrap-price and INR/USD volatility - now compounded by the US 25% reciprocal tariff on Indian imports effective August 1, 2025.

Customer, product and end-market concentration: top-3 customers were 22.98% of FY25 revenue, top-5 35.01% and top-10 52.78%; OEM/Tier-1 clients accounted for 77.13% of FY25 revenue; aluminium was 78.42% of the product mix; and the automotive end-market carries EV-transition risk (a shift away from aluminium castings could reduce demand).

FY24 loss dented net worth: a one-time non-cash goodwill write-off of Rs 1,239.63 cr (exceptional item) drove a FY24 loss (EPS -Rs 38.32) and reduced net worth from Rs 2,237.82 cr (FY23) to Rs 1,366.40 cr (FY24) before partial recovery to Rs 1,521.29 cr (FY25).

Extensive related-party dealings: recurring sales to and purchases from JV/associate and promoter-influenced entities (e.g. Nikkei MC Aluminium, Toyota Tsusho, Sanjivani Metal Trading), promoter remuneration and lease payments, and rent of Rs 26.70 cr (FY25) to Promoters for executive residence at The Camellias, Gurgaon.

Geographic and single-customer facility risk: facilities are clustered in north/west/south India (North India 57.67% of FY25 revenue) and the Bhiwadi and Odisha units are primarily dedicated to a single customer, with Bhiwadi sited on a customer's leased land.

High contract-labour intensity: 760 permanent employees versus 3,796 contractual workmen as of June 30, 2025 (attrition 17.32% FY25), with contract-labour-absorption and industrial-relations exposure (a past strike at the Chennai unit in January 2017).

parameter_scores.basis: Market leader at large scale (6,05,850 MTPA, Rs 6,666.49 cr FY25 revenue), but revenue CAGR is modest (~6.6% FY23-FY25); EBITDA growth stronger (Rs 207.01 -> 303.72 cr).
Headline RoNW 31.08% FY25 is strong versus peers, but margins are thin (EBITDA ~4.56%, PAT ~2.33%) and FY24 posted a loss (RoNW -265.9% as reported).
Operating cash flow was negative ~(Rs 92.00 cr) in FY25 despite PAT of Rs 155.04 cr; CFO has been volatile (Rs 610.90 cr FY23 -> Rs 74.10 cr FY24 -> negative FY25); year-end cash only Rs 1.77 cr.
Debt tripled to Rs 894.03 cr FY25 (31.75% of total assets) and net worth Rs 1,521.29 cr was dented by the FY24 goodwill write-off; D/E ~0.59x is still moderate and no promoter pledge exists.
Top-10 customers 52.78% and OEM/Tier-1 77.13% of FY25 revenue, aluminium 78.42% of product mix, no firm long-term contracts, and EV-transition / single-customer-facility exposure.

FY22-23 Qualified Opinion on unapproved JV related-party transactions plus non-maintenance of daily backup; pending Ugro Capital Section 7 IBC/CIRP application; untraceable historical share-transfer records; no CFO for ~11 months (Jun 2024-May 2025); several directors on struck-off companies; FY24 credit-rating downgrade; group JVs (CMRC/CCIIPL) on a non-going-concern basis with a SEBI exemption sought.

100% Offer for Sale of up to 42,890,735 shares - the Company receives no proceeds; investor Global Scrap Processors sells 23,178,450 of its 28,589,450 shares (~81% exit) alongside promoter selling shareholders; price band is [bullet] so P/E cannot be assessed (peers trade at 32.69x-82.70x).

red_flags: Insolvency proceeding: Ugro Capital initiated arbitration and a Section 7 IBC / CIRP application (approx. Rs 35.08 cr) before NCLT Chandigarh against the Company (refiled September 5, 2023, pending) over an alleged bill-discounting default, with an SLP pending before the Supreme Court and cross-default risk under other facilities.

Auditor Qualified Opinion (FY2022-23) on JV CMR Chiho Industries India Pvt Ltd relating to related-party transactions of Rs 39.30 cr and Rs 21.75 cr for which board approval was not taken (and Rs 5.46 cr not approved), plus non-maintenance of daily electronic backup of books; CARO 2020 adverse remarks on delayed statutory dues.

Group JVs CMRC and CCIIPL have been reported on a 'non-going-concern' basis since March 31, 2022 and, together with KAPL, did not provide the confirmations/undertakings required under SEBI ICDR - the Company has sought a SEBI exemption under Regulation 300(1)(c).

Untraceable historical corporate records, including share-transfer deeds dated July 30, 2007 among the Promoter Group, relied upon only via a practising company secretary's report - with no Chief Financial Officer appointed for the period June 6, 2024 to May 21, 2025.

Directors associated with struck-off companies: Mohan Agarwal (Nikkei CMR India Pvt Ltd, CTA Trading Pvt Ltd), Akshay Agarwal (Nikkei CMR India Pvt Ltd), Balvinder Kumar (Bharat Handloom Marketing Company Ltd), and Peter Francis Amour (AIF Capital (India) Pvt Ltd, though resigned before striking off).
Credit-rating downgrade in FY24: long-term rating cut to A+/Stable from AA-/Negative and short-term to CRISIL A1 from A1+ (both since reaffirmed).

Delayed payment of statutory dues (Provident Fund, GST, TDS) noted in the DRHP, with amounts subsequently paid; three past instances of one-day delays in debt servicing (including a minor delay with ICICI Bank).

100% Offer for Sale with no fresh issue: the Company receives no proceeds, and the offer is a monetisation event for the investor (Global Scrap Processors, exiting ~81% of its stake) and promoter selling shareholders; a FY24 buyback at Rs 135.58/share also returned capital to promoter-group and investor holders.
strengths_observed: Category leader: per the (commissioned) ICRA Report, CMR is India's leading non-ferrous metal recycler by installed capacity (as of March 31, 2025) and holds the highest market share in the Indian secondary aluminium market by FY2025 revenue among peers, with installed capacity around 4x the nearest domestic competitor, the largest recycled-liquid-aluminium supplier by turnover, and an estimated ~42-45% volume share of the automotive cast-alloy segment in FY2025.

Scale and footprint: 13 strategically located recycling facilities with combined installed capacity of 6,05,850 MTPA as of June 30, 2025, positioned adjacent to OEM/Tier-1 automotive clusters to supply molten liquid aluminium by road within a ~20-25 km radius on a just-in-time basis (patented ladle-transport technology).

Revenue growth with recovering profitability: revenue from operations rose from Rs 5,868.51 cr (FY23) to Rs 5,952.44 cr (FY24) to Rs 6,666.49 cr (FY25); EBITDA improved each year to Rs 303.72 cr (FY25) from Rs 217.40 cr (FY24) and Rs 207.01 cr (FY23); PAT recovered to Rs 155.04 cr in FY25 (EPS Rs 6.50) after a FY24 loss.

Strong headline return ratio: RoNW of 31.08% in FY25 - higher than three of the three DRHP-named listed peers (Pondy Oxides 9.79%, Gravita India 15.06%) and close to Baheti Recycling 30.46% - and the largest of the peer set by total income (Rs 6,696.66 cr vs Gravita Rs 3,980.61 cr, Pondy Rs 2,059.16 cr, Baheti Rs 524.54 cr).

Diversified global sourcing: metal scrap procured from around 198 suppliers across 73 countries (six continents), with a dedicated US sourcing subsidiary; India-sourced share of purchases rising to 26.85% in FY25 (FY24 19.69%, FY23 19.37%).

Strategic OEM alliances and technology tie-ups: long-standing Tier-1/OEM relationships (several spanning ten fiscals) and joint ventures with Toyota Tsusho (since 2012), Nikkei MC Aluminium (since 2012) and Nippon Light Metal (2025), supporting the entry into wrought-alloy / low-carbon extrusion billets.

ESG / decarbonisation positioning: recycling is far less energy-intensive than primary aluminium; the Company reports the 6th-highest S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment score among aluminium companies and holds ISO 14001, ISO 45001 and IATF 16949 certifications with a DSIR-recognised in-house R&D unit.

Clean promoter share pledge position: none of the Promoters' Equity Shares (nor the shares offered in the OFS) are pledged or otherwise encumbered as of the DRHP date; experienced founder-promoter (Chairman & MD Mohan Agarwal, over 31 years in aluminium recycling).
